Structural verification at head 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 against base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d confirms the claimed deletion. In integrations/claude/mod/hooks/register.js:144-161, dropQueued retains inflight objects but discardStale forms a Set of stale IDs and removes every queue object with those IDs. A passive invitation A enters pumpLazy at :543-550, which sets both its inflight flag and appendInflight. Child exit increments S.run and retains A (:197-213); startChild increments run again (:177-189). Neither child lifecycle path increments S.gen, so A's pending completion passes the gen guard at :564. After replacement status connected (:222-228), invitation B with the same ID but a different command_context_epoch produces a different contextVersion (:278-281), fails the invitation-specific duplicate predicate (:289-290), and is queued as a distinct current-run object. appendInflight prevents B from being appended (:544). A's eventual deny resets inflight, calls discardStale(batch,'late_deny') (:563-570), and removes both stale A and live B by their shared ID. No completion records B's context version, and the backoff/tick machinery cannot recreate an absent queue object. The success path deliberately removes invitation objects by identity (:327), which avoids this exact collision only for successful appends.

Refutation (a), present under another name: examined the relevant complete mod state machine, invitation/owner replay specifications, TRUST presentation rules, and canonical Watch emitter. The replacement stream's same-context duplicate refreshes A.run (:292), but that mechanism expressly does not match B's changed context. complete()'s identity removal is also absent from discardStale. Canonical replay is not a substitute for retaining B: src/cli/watch.rs:690-715 confirms a presentation immediately after stdout write/flush, independently of the asynchronous mod append; src/store/invitation_content.rs:949-960 retires confirmed noncontrol descriptors/outboxes. No mandatory reoffer of unchanged B after mod-side loss was found. The once-per-lease Watch owner replay correction addresses ordinary message offers, not invitation descriptors (resume-watch-owner-replay-design.md sections 3-4; TRUST-POLICY.md:1781-1815).

Refutation (b), accepted contract: TRUST-POLICY.md:1524-1528 explicitly limits invitation evidence to flushed physical output, not transcript/model uptake, and inherits A7 downstream silent-loss limits (:697-701). Those limits prevent claiming durable invitation loss or guaranteed model uptake. They do not permit an obsolete append result to discard a different already-received live-run context. The mod README's Routing rule retains denied appends for retry, and its Channel loss rule discards denied old inflight work unless the new run restreamed it. Existing delivery.test.ts:1099-1145 enforces preservation of restreamed work across a late denial; the new invitation multiple-context behavior breaks that preserved case. TRUST :1555-1557 and :1658-1662 allow transient revision coalescing but still describe eventual latest context after quiescence; B can be that sole latest renderable context. The accepted standalone render limits (:1748-1778) concern actual size failure, whereas this trace uses ordinary small renderable bodies and a stale refusal.

Refutation (c), scope: this is a single supported binding, two supported invitation contexts, and an ordinary watch restart; it requires no extra capacity, exactly-once semantics, transient-revision delivery, receipt ACK, or invitation acceptance guarantee. It is within the new context-epoch and passive invitation scheduling behavior.

Refutation (d), materiality: B disappears before any append attempt, so after a recoverable transport restart the current invitation instructions can remain absent from this mod's context even when the current channel and append API are usable. Canonical invitation/commands and explicit inspection remain available; no receipt or acceptance is synthesized. This is a significant delivery correctness regression, graded Should-fix rather than irreversible-data-loss Blocking.

Refutation (e), pre-existing: the base register.js has ID-wide discardStale at :153-159, but base onLine :250 admits only message/lazy/attention, rejects invitation kinds, and base :273-275 coalesces every same-ID queue object by refreshing its run. Therefore the stale-A/current-B invitation coexistence required for this defect is introduced by this diff, not a pre-existing defect to grade FYI. Refutation (f), linter territory: this is runtime queue identity/lifetime behavior, not formatting or style.
